CVE-2026-115864.title: Monoceros versions before 0.30 for Perl allow a request declaring a large Content-Length to kill a worker by exhausting memory
CVE-2026-115864.description:
Monoceros versions before 0.30 for Perl allow a request declaring a large Content-Length to kill a worker by exhausting memory.

The request body is read in a loop that asks sysread for all of the remaining declared length at once. Perl grows the read buffer to that size before any data arrives, so a length larger than available memory makes the worker exit with an uncatchable out of memory error before the application is called.

A remote attacker can force a worker restart with each request of a few bytes.

CVE-2026-117642.title: binary_to_term Stack Exhaustion via Nested Funs in NEW_FUN_EXT and EXPORT_EXT Aborts the VM
CVE-2026-117642.description:
Uncontrolled Recursion vulnerability in the external term format decoder in Erlang OTP erts allows an attacker who controls the input to binary_to_term/1,2 to abort the Erlang VM via a fun term with funs nested in its integer fields. dec_term in erts/emulator/beam/external.c decodes terms iteratively, except for the OldIndex and OldUniq fields of NEW_FUN_EXT and the Arity field of EXPORT_EXT. For these fields it calls itself, and it checks that the result is a small integer only after the call returns. An input that places another fun in such a field, nested to sufficient depth, recurses once per level, exhausts the stack of the scheduler thread and crashes the VM. The input must be large enough to reach that depth.

The abort takes down every process on the node. Supervision, try/catch and the safe option do not prevent it. enif_binary_to_term() and the distribution protocol reach the same decoder, and distribution is assumed to run on trusted networks only.

MISP contains an authorization bypass in its event search and filter functionality. CVE-2026-99663.title: mm/gup: fix clearing folios in memfd_pin_folios()
CVE-2026-99663.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/gup: fix clearing folios in memfd_pin_folios()

memfd_pin_folios() pins folios obtained directly from the page cache
without checking whether they are uptodate. However, shmem fallocate()
can leave newly allocated folios uncleared and not uptodate. Callers
such as udmabuf can then expose uninitialized memory to userspace.

Clear non-uptodate folios and mark them uptodate under the folio lock
before returning them to the caller.

Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private.
